content:
Bloomberg reported today that Apple is about to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware leasing programme, allowing users to subscribe to new Apple products with a monthly fee, but according to reports the programme has a limitation, which I hope ultimately will not come true.

"Apple Upgrade" will make higher-priced products more accessible, but entry-level models are reportedly excluded.

Due to the current AI-driven memory chip shortage, the prices of most Apple products have been raised recently.

Heading into autumn, this trend will further intensify, with new iPhone and Apple Watch models expected to see price hikes, not to mention the upcoming flagship iPhone Ultra and MacBook Ultra products.

According to Mark Gurman's report, Apple's response is to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware monthly subscription leasing option.

Gurman said the option will launch next week on the Apple online store and physical retail stores, and applies to in-store purchases.

Pending the final details, I think making Apple products more accessible in this way is a good thing.

The Apple Upgrade programme will be entirely voluntary, so any user who wants to purchase a product outright can still do so. But given the recent wave of price hikes, adding more options seems like the obvious move.

My only concern is the range of eligible hardware. Gurman noted that some devices will not be available through Apple Upgrade, including the "Apple Watch SE, entry-level iPad, iPhone 16 and MacBook Neo".

It would be a shame if Apple does not let users purchase its most affordable products through the leasing programme.

Imagine thinking Apple products are out of your reach, but with this new programme, a MacBook Neo could be yours for just US$20 a month. In such a case, Apple Upgrade has the potential to bring a large influx of new users into the Apple ecosystem.

I understand Apple wants to use this to push users towards higher-priced products, but limiting Apple Upgrade to specific hardware is an unnecessary move that only complicates the programme and limits its impact.

What do you think of the Apple Upgrade plan? Let us know in the comments.
